result.summary: This PR removes the FillableSigningProvider class from src/script/signingprovider.h/cpp, since its only real remaining user was LegacyDataSPKM (used for migrating legacy wallets) and its functionality is inlined directly into that class. All other users (unit tests, fuzz tests, benchmarks, and bitcoin-tx) are converted to use FlatSigningProvider instead, in some cases with explicit script insertion replacing the old implicit segwit-script learning. A related fix restricts signing of oversized (>520 byte) P2SH redeemScripts, since the old code could otherwise produce a consensus-invalid transaction.
result.problem: FillableSigningProvider was extracted from the legacy wallet years ago to build the SigningProvider abstraction, but with legacy wallet code removed elsewhere, keeping it as a separate class is unnecessary indirection that complicates the signing-provider hierarchy for maintainers and downstream code (tests, bitcoin-tx) that only used it out of convenience.

resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp found that the 520-byte script push limit wasn't enforced correctly for both P2SH and P2WSH after the FlatSigningProvider conversion in bitcoin-tx; achow101 added a commit enforcing it in signing.
jeanpablojp found LoadCScript vs AddCScript semantics differed (LoadCScript returns true without storing oversized scripts), causing the spkm_migration fuzz target to miscount; achow101 fixed it.
jeanpablojp noted script_sign fuzz target lost implicit P2WPKH script insertion and pubkey lookup that AddKey used to provide; achow101 restored the explicit insertions.

result.card: This PR removes the legacy FillableSigningProvider class from Bitcoin Core's signing-provider hierarchy, inlining its behavior directly into LegacyDataSPKM (the only real remaining user, for migrating legacy wallets) and converting all other users, tests, benchmarks, and the bitcoin-tx tool, to FlatSigningProvider. It is a cleanup that follows the prior removal of the legacy wallet, reducing an indirection layer that no longer has a reason to exist as its own class. During review, jeanpablojp and vicjuma manually tested the conversion and found real correctness bugs: bitcoin-tx could sign an oversized P2SH redeemScript into a consensus-invalid transaction, and two fuzz harnesses lost coverage or miscounted due to subtle AddCScript-versus-LoadCScript semantic differences; achow101 fixed all of them in follow-up commits. The PR now has concept and approach ACKs from three reviewers with no open objections, and the author remains active (last force-push 2026-09-14). No stated external dependency or blocking PR.
